STEP 1 - Scene: This is a simple fruit serving of cubed honeydew melon on a plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The vessel is a square white plate about 24 cm across. Treating it as a square of roughly 22 cm usable width gives an area of about 480 cm². For consistency with the circle formula, a 24 cm diameter gives 3.14 × 12² ≈ 452 cm², so I use about 450 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: The only visible food is honeydew melon cubes. There is also a tiny orange speck, which is negligible.

STEP 4 - Area: The melon covers about 20% of the plate, which is about 90 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: 90 cm² × 3 cm pile height = 270 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: 270 ml × 0.6 g/ml = 162 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Honeydew has about 36 kcal per 100 g, so 162 g gives about 58 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: There are about 14 cubes of roughly 2.5 cm each, at about 10–12 g per cube. That gives roughly 150–170 g, which matches the estimate.
